title: "People"
---

Every named director or staff member identified across the archive's history,
in one place. This list doubles as the working candidate list for oral-history
outreach; see [Sources & Open Questions](sources.qmd) for the status of that
effort. Living/availability status has not been checked for anyone below unless
noted.

::: {.callout-note}
## Libbie Stephenson: the single best-documented witness to this whole era
Her UCLA tenure runs almost exactly the length of the ISSR era itself: started
around 1977, the same year the archive was formally reconstituted as a named
ISSR unit, and continued through the 2014 Library transfer and two more years,
retiring in **2016**. BA Fine Arts (UC Riverside, 1975), MLS (UCLA, 1977).
IASSIST President 1995–97. ICPSR Council 1996–2000. Won the 2007 William H.
Flanigan Award for Distinguished Service as an ICPSR Official Representative,
and a 2016 IASSIST achievement award shortly before retiring. See
`evidence/stephenson-icpsr-sources.md`. **Correction**: an earlier note on this
site said 2014; that was wrong. Two independent primary sources (the retirement
article's own date stamp, and its reference to the 2016 IASSIST conference in
Bergen, Norway, confirmed independently) put it at 2016. She's very likely the
strongest oral-history candidate on this entire page: unlike Marvick or the
ISSR-era directors, she retired only a decade ago.
:::

## Notes

- Most pre-2014 names beyond Stephenson and Jamison come from a single
  deep-research pass and have not been independently verified against primary
  documents. See [Sources & Open Questions](sources.qmd).
- The distinction between "ISSR/SRC staff generally" and "SSDA-specific staff" is
  often unclear in the sourcing. Several names above may have served the parent
  institute broadly rather than the archive specifically.
- Several 2014–present entries above rest partly on Tim's own direct recollection
  as a participant, not yet cross-checked against a document. That's a different,
  valid kind of source (oral testimony from someone who was there), not a lesser
  one, but it's marked separately from publicly documented facts so the two don't
  blur together.
